summary: Connected lan-a (10.10.10.0/24) and lan-b (10.20.20.0/24) through routed VyOS wg01 interfaces (10.255.255.0/30). Node3 serves the application at 10.10.10.10:8080; node4 reaches it from 10.20.20.10. Only new TCP/8080 connections to that application are permitted cross-LAN, established/related replies are allowed, and NAT is not configured. All four nodes passed sequential reboot-persistence verification.
actions_performed: Generated active WireGuard keys locally on each gateway and saved the VyOS configuration.
Configured opposing LAN routes through wg01 and persistent host routes through each gateway.
Installed and enabled the node3 application service bound to 10.10.10.10:8080.
Applied default-drop VyOS forwarding policies allowing only new lan-b-to-application TCP/8080 traffic.
Verified allowed application access, denied SSH attempts in both cross-LAN directions, WireGuard handshakes, and firewall counters.
Restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 individually; verified changed boot IDs and complete recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: Routed WireGuard connectivity through wg01 without address translation
evidence.summary: Both gateways show wg01 addresses, reciprocal LAN routes, active peers with traffic counters, hidden private keys, and “NAT is not configured.”

evidence.requirement: Node3 application on TCP 8080 is reachable from node4 through the tunnel
evidence.summary: Node3 shows the enabled active listener at 10.10.10.10:8080 and its data hash; node4 routes via 10.20.20.1 and receives “lan-a application.”

evidence.requirement: New cross-LAN connections are limited to the application path
evidence.summary: SSH probes time out in both directions. Gateway policies allow only new TCP traffic to 10.10.10.10:8080, allow established/related traffic, and record default-policy drops.
